title: Interacting with Zscaler Client Connector Remotely

blocks.text: This feature is available only for Zscaler Client Connector version 4.4 and later for Windows and Zscaler Client Connector version 4.3 and later for macOS. Some options require later versions of Zscaler Client Connector for Windows.
You can use a CLI to interact with Zscaler Client Connector remotely to do the following:

blocks.item: View the status of services.
Enable or disable the Private Access (ZPA) service.
Enable or disable the Internet & SaaS (ZIA) service and the Digital Experience (ZDX) service (Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 and later for Windows only).
Update installation parameters without reinstalling Zscaler Client Connector (Zscaler Client Connector version 4.9 and later for Windows only).
Upgrade the Digital Experience (ZDX) Module for Windows (Zscaler Client Connector version 4.7 and later for Windows only).

blocks.text: This feature is useful if you must interact with services on behalf of users (for example, an outage requires you to disable Private Access for all users).
You can enable the CLI for the following OSs:

blocks.item: Windows
To enable the CLI for Windows devices:
From the navigation menu, go to Infrastructure > Client Connector > Windows.
On the App Profiles tab, click Add Windows Policy. The Add Windows Policy window appears.
In the Command Line Interface Access section of the Add Windows Policy window, enable the Command Line Interface.
Click Save.
Optionally, you can require a password when disabling a service using the CLI.
To require a password when disabling the Private Access, Internet & SaaS, or Digital Experience service:
If you're adding a new policy, you must first save your policy before generating a password.
If you're editing an existing policy, you must first save your changes before generating a password.
In the Disable Services section, do one of the following:
Enable Disable ZPA Password to require a password when disabling the Private Access service using the CLI.
The Generate ZPA Disable Password option appears.
Enable Disable ZIA Password to require a password when disabling the Internet & SaaS service using the CLI.
The Generate ZIA Disable Password option appears.
Enable Disable ZDX Password to require a password when disabling the ZDX service using the CLI.
The Generate ZDX Disable Password option appears.
Click Generate Password to generate a password. The generated password displays in the associated Generate <Service> Disable Password field.
Click Copy to copy the password to your clipboard. The password expires after two hours.
macOS
To enable the CLI for macOS devices:
From the navigation menu, go to Infrastructure > Client Connector > macOS.
On the App Profiles tab, click Add macOS Policy. The Add macOS Policy window appears.
In the Command Line Interface Access section of the Add macOS Policy window, enable the Command Line Interface.
Click Save.
Optionally, you can require a password when disabling a service using the CLI.
To require a password when disabling the Private Access, Internet & SaaS, or Digital Experience service:
If you're adding a new policy, you must first save your policy before generating a password.
If you're editing an existing policy, you must first save your changes before generating a password.
In the Disable Services section, do one of the following:
Enable Disable ZPA Password to require a password when disabling the Private Access service using the CLI.
The Generate Password option appears.
Enable Disable ZIA Password to require a password when disabling the Internet & SaaS service using the CLI.
The Generate Password option appears.
Enable Disable ZDX Password to require a password when disabling the Digital Experience service using the CLI.
The Generate Password option appears.
Click Generate Password to generate a password. The generated password displays in the associated Generate Password field.
Click Copy to copy the password to your clipboard. The password expires after two hours.

blocks.text: You can use the CLI for the following OSs:

blocks.item: Windows
To use CLI for Windows devices:
Start a command prompt as an administrator.
Use one of the following file paths, depending on your Windows system version:
For 64-bit: C:\Program Files\Zscaler\ZSACli\ZSACli.exe <command>
For 32-bit: C:\Program Files (x86)\Zscaler\ZSACli\ZSACli.exe <command>
Replace <command> with one of the following commands and press Enter.

table: Possible values for <service>: zia (indicates Internet & SaaS) zpa (indicates Private Access) zdx (indicates Digital Experience) If you are enabling Private Access for a partner tenant, add -u <partner username> after zpa. Can be run five or fewer times per minute.

Possible values for <service>: zia (indicates Internet & SaaS) zpa (indicates Private Access) zdx (indicates Digital Experience) If you enabled Disable <Service> Password and generated a password in app profiles, add -p <disable password> after <service>. Example: ZSAcli.exe disable -s zpa -p <disable password> Can be run three or fewer times per minute.
Display the status in a JSON format of the entered service, or for all services if you enter all.

Possible values for <service>: zia (indicates Internet & SaaS) zpa (indicates Private Access) zdx (indicates Digital Experience) deception (indicates Zscaler Deception) zep (indicates Anti-Tampering) all (indicates all services)
Update the specified installation parameter with the new value.

Possible values for <parameter name>: cloudName deviceToken externalDeviceId policyToken strictEnforcement userDomain bcpConfigFilePath To learn more about the parameters in the list, see Supported Parameters for Zscaler Client Connector for Windows. To view the parameters available for updating and the current value (if set), enter params -list. To view a specific parameter and its value (if set), enter params -get <parameter name>. Can be run five or fewer times per minute.
Displays help information about the CLI arguments.
Upgrades the ZDX Module with the update package in the path you enter.
You must first enable ZDX Module upgrades from the CLI. You can download the package and copy the checksum on the Client Connector App Store page.
Upgrades the ZDX Module with the update package located at the URL you enter.
You must first enable ZDX Module upgrades from the CLI. You can download the package and copy the checksum on the Client Connector App Store page.

blocks.item: If a message displays indicating that the CLI is disabled from the policy, enable the Command Line Interface option in the app profile.
macOS
To use CLI for macOS devices:
Start a command prompt as an administrator.
Use the following file path:
/Applications/Zscaler/Zscaler.app/Contents/PlugIns/zscli <command>
Replace <command> with one of the following commands and press Enter.

table: Possible values for <service>: zia (indicates Internet & SaaS) zpa (indicates Private Access) zdx (indicates Digital Experience) If you are enabling Private Access for a partner tenant, add -u <partner username> after zpa. Can be run five or fewer times per minute.

Possible values for <service>: zia (indicates Internet & SaaS) zpa (indicates Private Access) zdx (indicates Digital Experience) If you enabled Disable <Service> Password and generated a password in app profiles, add -p <disable password> after <service>. Example: zscli disable -s zpa -p <disable password> Can be run three or fewer times per minute.
Display the status in a JSON format of the entered service, or for all services if you enter all.

Possible values for <service>: zia (indicates Internet & SaaS) zpa (indicates Private Access) zdx (indicates Digital Experience) zdp (indicates Endpoint Data Loss Prevention) all (indicates all services)
Displays help information about the CLI arguments.
Possible examples for help: zscli -h zscli enable -h zscli disable -h zscli status -h
Runs diagnostics for Zscaler Client Connector and outputs a file location for the diagnostics.

blocks.item: If a message displays indicating that the CLI is disabled from the policy, enable the Command Line Interface option in the app profile.
